accuracy.evidence: Checked against AQA GCSE Chemistry 8462 sections 4.6.1.2 to 4.6.1.4 (collision theory, activation energy, effect of concentration, pressure, surface area, temperature and catalysts), Edexcel topic 7 and NGSS HS-PS1-5. The lab model draws particle speeds from the Maxwell distribution at the set kelvin temperature, keeps it there with a water-bath thermostat, counts each first contact once and reacts only when line-of-centres energy reaches Ea, so heating raises hits by about a tenth but successes by far more, as the text claims.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented rate slips: every collision reacts (step 1 prediction and p1), temperature works only through collision frequency (step 2 prediction, size tag, m2), heating lowers Ea (eaT tag), crowding makes collisions harder (energy and speed tags, step 3 prediction, m5), powder is hotter or has a lower Ea (hot and eaS tags, p3), a catalyst adds energy or is used up (catE and used tags, m3), and the cold stops particles (stop tag, m7).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcoll is the only lab with a slingshot that fires one reactant particle at another against an activation energy bar, plus a live two-reactant particle box with temperature, concentration and catalyst dials, a results table of repeated 10 second tests and a collision energy histogram with a movable Ea line. gaslab and flagtemp show particle motion and pressure but never count successful collisions or show Ea.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step isolates one variable with a fair test the learner runs: bounce versus react, 20 °C versus 60 °C or hotter at the same concentration, two concentrations at one temperature, catalyst off versus on with all else fixed, then a target of 600 reactions per run that needs all three. The done messages quote the learner's own numbers of hits and successes and name which factor changed.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions come before the evidence: whether every collision reacts, the main reason heating works (with the lower-Ea distractor), whether the successful share changes with concentration, and how a catalyst works. Each is checked by the very next test the learner runs, and the reveal compares the prediction with the table rows.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions cover the fridge, the 10 °C rule, concentration, powder versus lump and the catalyst. Each wrong choice carries its own tag and a specific reply that names the error, for example that Ea belongs to the reaction route so heating cannot change it, or that powder wins on surface area and not on temperature.

readability.evidence: Learner text uses short sentences and defines activation energy, successful collision and rate of reaction on first use, keeping the grade level within the validator limit. Adult notes give exam board references, a key terms list, the main misconceptions with classroom moves, a note on the model's small Ea and a marble chips follow-up practical.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph carries a testable claim: the two conditions for reaction, the definition of rate, the three frequency factors, the two effects of heat and the catalyst pathway. The practice set uses real calculations of successful collisions from percentages, mean rate from gas volume and mass, and the doubling rule, with no padding items.

mobile.evidence: The canvas keeps a 0.66 ratio with a tall option on phones, the particle box scales to the width with a minimum dot radius, and all dials are large button twins below the canvas in a wrapping control row. The results table shows only the last six tests so it fits a phone screen, and tests run synchronously so the page never stalls.

accessibility.evidence: The slingshot has Gentle push and Hard push button twins, every dial is a labelled button with aria-pressed for toggles, the canvas aria-label and a polite live region read out each test result in words, the challenge uses real buttons with a status region, and colours come from the theme palette so contrast holds in light and dark themes.

sources: AQA (2016, current) GCSE Chemistry specification 8462, 4.6.1 Rate of reaction: collision theory and activation energy, catalysts
Pearson Edexcel GCSE Chemistry 1CH0, topic 7 Rates of reaction and energy changes
